To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the health system implications and the health system response to advances in genetics and genomic medicine are not yet clear and that targeted research on the health services and policy implications of genetics and genomics is needed to help decision-makers at all level of the health system understand and address this issue.

the Helix in the labyrinth is a metaphor that describes how genetics and genomics are changing health care and the health system, and that genetic health services and policy researchers will play a crucial, but as yet undefined, role in guiding the health system through this labyrinth.

genetic health services and policy researchers are needed to inform decision makers at all levels of our health system about whether, and how, to integrate genetics and genomics and other new complex health technologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a research agenda for the health system implications and health services research aspects of genetics and genomics in Canada.
the health system implications, and potential benefits and risks, of genetic and genomic research and development.
understanding the implications of genetic and genomic research on the organization, delivery, financing and evaluation of health care in Canada.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genetic HSPR is needed, but it is not clear what it should be.
the need for HSPR in genetic health services and policy is a matter of debate.
genetic and genomic HSPR is necessary but insufficient for the effective integration of these technologies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Helix in the Labrynth is a very important one.
we need to know more before we can know less.
genetic health services and policy (HSP) research is needed to inform health policy and practice in Canada and elsewhere.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HSPR community needs to be prepared to respond to the health system implications and opportunities of genetic and genomic research and technologies.
the health system implications are not yet clear, and that the HSPR community needs to be engaged in the development of a new research program to help clarify these implications.
genetic HSPR should be seen as a subset of the broader HSPR enterprise, and should not be developed or conducted in isolation.
